Expansion Post
[spoiler=Angjas, Terakhia and Ghijand]
The first archaeological evidence of settlement within either Angjas or Terakhia were found within the Qarijan Archaeological Site, where ancient artifacts such as preserved stone tools, intricately carved rocks and even a number of bones from ancient mammals were discovered within the site. The Qarijan site is considered the oldest known archaeological evidence of society within southern Alaqar, being estimated at around fifteen thousand years old. Much details of life 15,000 years ago were found within the remains and the surrounding area. Ancient Alaqans were likely a farming based society, with evidence showing rough tools shaped from bone that were likely used as hoes or shovels for digging into the earth. Others disagree, saying the bone tools were probably weapons, perhaps weapons to hunt some of the megafauna that roamed Alaqar thousands of years ago.

The first hints of a true civilization within the eastern highlands came upon the rise of the Urtics, a people estimated to have came to Erene at around 2000 BCE. These ancient people have much preserved evidence of their existence, coming from ancient ruins, burial sites or old texts describing the existence of the Urctics. These texts often stated that the Urctics were a hardy, nomadic people, skilled upon horseback and experienced with spears and harpoons. Remains of the Urctics show that they took great care of their weapons, with many having taken the time to carve decorations into the spearhead and shaft. Many archaeologists have suggested that warriors and horsemen took a high standing within Urctic society, seen perhaps as an honor and worthy of recognition and praise and thus were treated as a nobility of sorts. The Urctics rarely wrote down sagas of their civilization, as they seemingly lacked a cohesive writing system. Most Urctic texts were simply drawings of various objects and things, such as goats, horses, cows, or other common game animals. What is preserved still gave a very important look into the early history of the Alaqan east. 

The Urctics were followed by the Feziliks, a more civilized and less nomadic than their predecessors. The Feziliks were much more of a farming society than the Urctics were, concentrating most of their population along the river Angjas, a river that funneled into the Shamatine Strait. The Feziliks were responsible for founding the modern day city of Namanhiq, today the capital of Terakhia. The river was essential for Fezilik society, as it both gave them a source of water in the otherwise dry climate for both drinking and farming, and it allowed for trade via sailing down river into said strait, albeit trade was limited due to sheer distance and the rough geography. The Feziliks were at first disunited and often fought between each other for resources, food or simply for power amongst warlords.

Over east of the Shaki mountains, a group from the far north of East Shamat  had arrived within the Valley of Ghijand and made its home there around the year 400 CE. The Ghijandis are thought to have originated from the areas around modern-day Aekarxa, a Hydronian province, but finding evidence for the origins of Ghijand has proven difficult even in the modern day. These peoples were escaping from a devastating winter that left what little crops they could grow in shambles. Upon mixing with the locals already within the Valley of Ghijand, the valley broke up into bitter warlord groups and clans that fought for resources within Ghijand. Eventually, one warlord, a skilled warrior by the name of Toychi, established the Kingdom of Ghijand after uniting the clans within the valley, whether by force, diplomacy or bribery. The kingdom made its capital in Nursah, the most prominent town within Ghijand at the time and the modern capital of the province today.

Around the year 550 BCE, a local warlord by the name of Jora led an impressive campaign down the Angjas river, raiding and capturing villages and supplies. The warlords states raided were subjugated under Joras rule, while those who  were left alone either joined under threat or were conquered by Joras army. A kingdom was established that stretched across both modern day Terakhia and Angjas, known simply as the Joran Empire. The empire was a major power within what is today Alaqar, with a strong and modern army as well as a cunning leader at the helm. Jora lived till about 50 years old when he died and his son, Jora II, took the reins of power. His son was just as cunning as his father and made expansive reforms to the kingdom, expanding its borders across the plains all the way up to the Shamatine Strait and even stretching across the Shaki Mountains. However, the kingdom had stretched its resources too far, as well as caused destruction to the nearby realms that refused to bend to it, and it only took Joras unexpected death to shatter it to pieces. The heir to the throne, Jora the Third, was only about 9 years old around this time, and his claim to the throne was being pressed and pushed by the various nobles and aristocrats that made up the kingdoms elite inner circle. A coup attempt was made by an even aristocrat whose name is lost to time, a move which essentially shattered the crowns legitimacy within some of its vassal states, said states which were only kept under the Joran Empires sphere by royal marriage. The Joran Empire crumbled into numerous small warlords almost overnight, battling for what was left of the kingdom. The Terakhs and Angjians both fell into internal chaos, however with the continued collapse of their former overlord, the unrest seeping through both kingdoms quickly died down. While under the Joran Empire, some of the various peoples within had intermixed together and formed something of a close identity between each other. However, Angjas and Terakhia, which were both within the hearts of the Joran Empire, kept their Fezilik heritage alive. It mattered very little, as the warlord states simply vied for personal power over any sense of unification. 

Hundreds and hundreds of years would pass, crossing into the Common Era and into the 13th century. The warlord states had become fully fledged kingdoms at this point, about 8 or so kingdoms were still fighting between each other, just as a kingdom in the far north known as simply Hydronia was taking shape. To prevent themselves from potentially being overrun and to end the persistent fighting, the kingdoms within what is today Alaqar met together in what is called the Convention of Sarytagan. This convention included Terakhia but didnt include Angjus due to a lack of interest from Angjuss government. Ghijand merely sat by, unbothered by the goings-on of the states across the Shaki mountains. This meeting turned out to be a huge success, with the kings agreeing to form a sort of confederation of their respective kingdoms. The confederation was initially a success, helping foster economic development and social reforms within Alaqar. However, one of the top generals of the confederation, General Badai, launched a coup of the government in November of 1267. General Badai went to work immediately, strengthening the central governments authority and preparing the army for an offensive war. 

In 1268, he began his legendary 7 year campaign, placing his one son in charge of the throne as Khan of Alaqar and heading east with his army in what is called the March East. He was an effective, calculating and terrifying figure, wise when it came to battle decisions and planning and fearless in battle. He first invaded Angjus, which to its credit, held up an impressive defense considering the size and numbers difference between Alaqar and Angjus. After managing to break through Angjus defensive lines, he laid siege to its capital city of Chirkent. The kingdom of Angjus wailed to nearby Ghijand for its help, however Ghijand ignored these calls. Ghijand was under the impression that Badai would not venture across the Shaki Mountains, hoping to merely sit by as Alaqar rose and eventually fell again. Despite heavy resistance from Angjus, it fell within about 6 months of fighting, and was turned into a new province of Alaqar. After this initial success in Angjus, General Badai got bold and quickly regrouped his armies, aiming them on an eastern path for his famed campaign. In the fall of 1267, he moved his army across the Shaki Mountains and struck into the eastern steppes. General Badai went forward on with his conquest, aiming for Ghijand first, a state which Badai thought would be an easy grab. He was briefly mistaken, as Ghijand put up a strong defense and managed to briefly push Badai back across the mountains. These successes would not last, as Badai regrouped and overwhelmed the Ghijandis with sheer numbers and expert flanking tactics. Things for Alaqar were initially going well, as they were beginning to see profits from their eastern raids that helped fund their army. However, General Badai had made the same mistake that the Jorans from 700 years ago made: he had overstretched his army and had given Alaqar way more land than it could realistically keep under control or effectively govern. General Badai was brave to a fault in battle, so much so that he died 7 years into his campaign from a well placed shot to the knee causing him to fall off his horse and die of trampling. This meant that the son that was back home to run things was now the new Khan. The army preformed a hurried retreat back across the Shaki mountains to Shiganuur, in what is called the Mad Dash West. His dynasty tried to keep the empire of Badai together, however internal tensions and unrest sealed the fate of the empire for years to come.

Badais empire slowly folded in on itself as the 13th, 14th and 15th centuries went by. Ghijand broke away from Alaqar during the Second Fracturing, using its distance from the main population centers of Alaqar along the coast and its geographical terrain to irs advantage. Ghijand won the ensuing war and became an independent kingdom once more. Upon the beginning of the First Hydronian Defense, where the Holy Hydronic Empire attempted to subjugate the weakened Alaqan state, the Ghijandis raised a mercenary group and sold off mercenaries to both the Hydronian and Alaqan militaries. The two powers didnt complain over Ghijand playing both sides, as long as the state stayed neutral in their affair. Ghijand benefited greatly economically from the exchange for the First, Second and Third Hydronian Defenses, when Ghijand shipped out mercenaries for all three wars.

The Final Fracturing led to the First Alaqan Khanate finally breaking apart in 1429. In the Final Fracturing, Angjas and Terakhia took their chances and seceded from Alaqar. The Alaqan Khanate was unable to prevent their secession as the khanate quickly broke down into the original warring kingdoms that first formed the confederation. For about a hundred years after the Final Fracturing, Angjas and Terakhia were free to choose their own destiny.

Angjas and Terakhia diplomatically got along well, thanks to their shared Fezilik roots and their shared control over the Angjas river. Their control over the Angjas river allowed them to influence the richer and more trade connected kingdoms bordering the Shamatine Strait. Namanhiq especially, the capital of Terakhia, went through an extensive reformation of social order and economic restructuring led by King Batir the Humble. Along with these reforms, Fezilik culture flourished within Namanhiq and by proxy the rest of Terakhia. The citys new policies were a major success, quickly becoming one of the most important and prosperous cities within the broken remains of Alaqar. Its location along the river Angjus allowed it to become a major trading destination during the period between the Fracturings and Reunification. King Batir had put his capital of Namanhiq on the path to becoming one of Alaqars most important and prosperous cities for years to come.

However, the broken kingdoms of Alaqar would eventually come to blows in the year 1540, a war brought about by a web of alliances and an inner desire to reunite Alaqar under their respective banners. Angjus and Terakhia banded together in a multi-sided war between various ethnicities and factions, all vying for the throne of the Khan. The two Fezilik powers achieved a number of military successes thanks to their dry climate and higher elevation, however as the war dragged on their successes were halted and famine began to overtake the country. Before the effects of famine could truly overwhelm the nation, however, the war ended in a truce as King Kodir the Second of Terakhia chose to surrender and join the larger Unitary Front, an alliance that had succeeded in securing most of the nation and was close to fully restored the Khanate. When Terakhia surrendered, Angjus found itself surrounded on three sides by a larger enemy army, and chose to surrender instead of throwing men at a lost cause.

The two kingdoms were folded into the new Second Khanate of Alaqar, however were kept as separate provinces instead of being merged for governing efficiency. Despite their initial fighting against the new Alaqan state, the annexation proved to have a positive effect upon the two states. Funding from Alaqar helped clean and polish the two provinces, allowing for increased economic and recovery from many years of chaos and conflict. Ghijand was left alone by the Alaqan state, with Alaqar not wanting to risk overstretching themselves like in their past conflicts. In 1587, Ghijand revolutionized its government by introducing a parliamentary assembly. This parliament had many powers, but its most prominent role was to balance the powers of the monarch and itself. This change would be a major factor in Alaqars revolution in 1617. In the Alaqan Revolution of 1617, masses of peasants within the country rose up against the absolutist monarchy ruling Alaqar. The revolution was surprisingly peaceful for its size, thanks to the high peasantry population in the capital city, Shiganuur. The Shigan people surrounded the most important government buildings armed with pitchforks, hammers, and various weapons ready to fight, however the government conceded to the peoples demands, not wishing to potentially lose their own lives for the sake of the Khans power. Angjus, Terakhia and Ghijand were all in support for the constitutional government, with Angjus and Terakhia specifically seeing it as an opportunity to gain autonomy from the Alaqan Khanate.

After the revolution, Ghijand and Alaqar were left in relative peace for about 70 years. This period of peace was met with solid development of both sides economies and relations, however it would come to a close in 1677. In 1677, Alaqar intervened in the Sultanate of Bozor, a kingdom which had been ravaged by war for the better part of a few years at this point. Alaqar took advantage of the opportunity and annexed the sultanate into Alaqar, and the Khan approved a second invasion into Ghijand as an attempt to shock them and leave the Ghijandis incapable of defense. This was not the case, as once again, Ghijand sent the Alaqan army of 40,000 running across the Shaki mountains. The Alaqans were beaten so bad that the governors of the nearby provinces called to the Khan for help from the much smaller Ghijandi army. The next 150 years consisted of a long lasting peace within Alaqar and Ghijand, minus Alaqars invasion of Hydronia in 1728 and the Islamic Revolution of 1800. Ghijand and Alaqar had been hosting talks in the dawn of the 19th century over a possible unification of the two states. These talks would eventually succeed, and Ghijand would join the Second Khanate of Alaqar in January of 1829. The rest of the 19th century would turn out to be a major economic miracle for Angjus, Terakhia and Ghijand together. The three provinces grew quickly both economically and in population. This growth was only further bolstered by the rising value of crude oil, something which was being discovered in more and more sites across the country.

The 20th century was even more wild for Alaqar and its provinces. When the Great War had broken out and Erene essentially caught on fire, Alaqar remained a neutral state as numerous countries surrounding it such as Llyndora and Nordiheim joined the war. Alaqar benefited greatly from the war from an economic standpoint, shipping out oil and other valuable goods to warring nations to make a hefty profit. These profits often went to oil-producing states such as Terakhia, Angjus and Ghijand, states who were already benefiting greatly from its rising value. The Second World War was different, however, as Alaqar joined the war on an imperialist campaign, led by a particularly eccentric and ambitious Khan at the helm. Although Alaqar had initially claimed victories in its Shamatine War, some of the more industrial provinces were paying the price from bombing raids and air attacks upon key infrastructure and industrial facilities. After the war, the three provinces went under an economic recovery under the new Khatun, Mÿra, and her guidance. The three provinces today are considered some of Alaqars most industrious and most prosperous provinces thanks to their natural resources, solid history and low corruption rates, helping contribute to Alaqars rising power as one of Shamats great powers.[/spoiler]
